Reference / os/port

os/port#

Code in any language, called from Okkama through a helper process (#1081): the Erlang "ports" model.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

import "os/command" take InheritedCommand;
import "fs/path" take Path;
import "json" take Json, JsonField;

async main() is int {
    let images = Port(command: InheritedCommand(program: Path("bin/image-helper")));
    let thumb = await images.call(method: "resize", payload: Json(JsonField("width", 200)), bytes: [byte(137)]);
    let size = thumb.json().int("bytes");
    images.close();
    0;
}

Description#

Code in any language, called from Okkama through a helper process (#1081): the Erlang "ports" model. A helper is a program that reads framed requests on its standard input and writes framed replies on its standard output (docs/port-protocol.md); okkama-port is the Rust crate that writes the helper side in a few lines.

  • A helper starts with the first call, not when the port is made. One that ends, crashes, breaks the protocol or does not answer in time is stopped, the calls waiting on it fail with a PortFailure, and the next call starts a fresh one. A helper's failure never takes the program down.
  • Calls carry ids, so many may be in flight at once on one helper, and replies may come in any order.
  • Each call has a timeout (30 seconds unless told otherwise); it covers starting the helper when one is needed. A call that times out stops its helper, as a hung helper would hold up every call after it.
  • instances: N keeps up to N helpers, and a call goes to the one with the fewest calls in flight.
  • Payloads are JSON (Json) or CBOR (Cbor), chosen per call; the reply comes in the codec of its request. Raw bytes travel beside the payload in frames of their own, without base64.

The helper's standard error is free for its logs: the port keeps its last 2 KiB for the failure of a crashed helper. A helper is found by its command's program path: a path with a directory runs that file, a bare name is looked up in PATH. Blade does not carry helper binaries yet; a program names the path of one it built or installed.

Public API#

enum PortCodec#

enum PortCodec = (json, cbor)

The codec of a call's payload, and of its reply.

  • json: JSON text, which every helper accepts.
  • cbor: CBOR, for helpers that name it in their hello.

PortCodec.json#

json

JSON text, which every helper accepts.

PortCodec.cbor#

cbor

CBOR, for helpers that name it in their hello.

object Port#

object Port

Helper processes that answer calls: started with the first call, restarted after a crash or a hang.

import "os/command" take InheritedCommand;
import "fs/path" take Path;
import "json" take Json, JsonField;

async main() is int {
    let text = Port(command: InheritedCommand(program: Path("bin/text-helper")), instances: 2);
    let words = await text.call("words", Json(JsonField("text", "to be or not")));
    let count = words.json().int("count");
    text.close();
    0;
}

Port.Port#

Port(command is Commanding, instances is int = 1, frame_limit is int = 16777216)

Up to instances helpers run by command; a frame from a helper may be frame_limit bytes (16 MiB unless told otherwise).

Port.call#

async call(method is string, payload is Json = Json(), bytes is @byte = [], timeout is Duration = Duration(seconds: 30.rat())) is PortReply

The helper's answer to method with a JSON payload and raw bytes; PortFailure when the helper refuses, crashes, hangs past timeout or breaks the protocol.

Port.call#

async call(method is string, payload is Cbor, bytes is @byte = [], timeout is Duration = Duration(seconds: 30.rat())) is PortReply

The helper's answer to method with a CBOR payload and raw bytes; the helper must accept CBOR, or the call is PortFailure.unsupported.

Port.close#

close() is void

Stops every helper; calls in flight fail with PortFailure.closed, and so does every later call. Closing again does nothing.

object PortReply#

object PortReply

What a helper answered: its payload in the codec of the request, and the raw bytes it attached.

import "os/command" take InheritedCommand;
import "fs/path" take Path;

async main() is int {
    let hashes = Port(command: InheritedCommand(program: Path("bin/hash-helper")));
    let reply = await hashes.call(method: "digest", bytes: [byte(1), byte(2)]);
    let hex = reply.json().text("hex");
    let raw = reply.bytes();
    hashes.close();
    0;
}

PortReply.PortReply#

PortReply(codec is PortCodec, json is Json, cbor is Cbor, attachments is @@byte)

Made by Port.call(); not constructed directly.

PortReply.json#

json() is Json

The payload of a reply to a JSON call (null when the helper sent none); PortFailure.wrong_codec for a CBOR call.

PortReply.cbor#

cbor() is Cbor

The payload of a reply to a CBOR call (null when the helper sent none); PortFailure.wrong_codec for a JSON call.

PortReply.bytes#

bytes() is @byte

The raw bytes the helper attached, joined in order; [] when none.

Errors#

enum PortFailure#

enum PortFailure is Error = (unavailable(command is string, reason is string), incompatible(protocol is int), unsupported(codec is PortCodec), timed_out(method is string), crashed(method is string, detail is string), malformed(method is string, reason is string), refused(method is string, code is string, message is string), wrong_codec(asked is PortCodec, answered is PortCodec), closed)

Why a call to a helper failed.

  • unavailable: The helper could not be started (the command and why).
  • incompatible: The helper speaks another protocol version than 1.
  • unsupported: The helper does not accept this codec.
  • timed_out: No answer in time; the helper was stopped.
  • crashed: The helper ended or was stopped before it answered; detail says how it ended and what it last wrote on its standard error.
  • malformed: The helper broke the protocol; it was stopped.
  • refused: The helper answered with a failure: its code and message.
  • wrong_codec: The reply was asked for in one codec and came in another.
  • closed: The port is closed.

PortFailure.unavailable#

unavailable(command is string, reason is string)

The helper could not be started (the command and why).

PortFailure.incompatible#

incompatible(protocol is int)

The helper speaks another protocol version than 1.

PortFailure.unsupported#

unsupported(codec is PortCodec)

The helper does not accept this codec.

PortFailure.timed_out#

timed_out(method is string)

No answer in time; the helper was stopped.

PortFailure.crashed#

crashed(method is string, detail is string)

The helper ended or was stopped before it answered; detail

PortFailure.malformed#

malformed(method is string, reason is string)

The helper broke the protocol; it was stopped.

PortFailure.refused#

refused(method is string, code is string, message is string)

The helper answered with a failure: its code and message.

The reply was asked for in one codec and came in another.
